items.title: Flow calculus of a self-adjoint generator: commutation, invariance and differentiability
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral and functional-calculus suppliers. Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $T$ be self-adjoint on $H$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) with spectral projection-valued measure $E$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and put
$$U(t):=e^{itT}=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{it\lambda}\,dE(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R)$$
in the sense of the integral of a measurable function against a projection-valued measure ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]). Then:

(a) $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]) with $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$ and $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ for all $s,t$; moreover $U(t)D(T)=D(T)$, $TU(t)=U(t)T$ on $D(T)$, and the difference quotient $\frac1t\bigl(U(t)x-x\bigr)$ has a norm limit as $t\to0$ exactly for $x\in D(T)$, where that limit is $iTx$ ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]], [[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]).

(b) For every bounded Borel function $h:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$ one has $h(T)U(t)=U(t)h(T)$; in particular $E(B)U(t)=U(t)E(B)$ for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$.

(c) For $x\in D(T)$ the map $t\mapsto U(t)x$ is differentiable at every $t\in\mathbb R$, with
$$\frac{d}{dt}U(t)x=iU(t)Tx=iTU(t)x;$$
for $x\in H\setminus D(T)$ the map $t\mapsto U(t)x$ is differentiable at no point of $\mathbb R$.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Theorems 5.1-5.2, printed pages 123-125 (a self-adjoint operator generates a strongly continuous unitary group; the derivative exists exactly on the domain and equals iT)
B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Sections 2.1-2.3, printed pages 10-17 (unitary time evolution, the evolution operator and the generator equation)

items.title: Heisenberg flow of a bounded operator: conjugates, covariance and the equation of motion
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $T$ be self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) and $U(t)=e^{itT}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]]; for $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) put
$$A(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$
Then:

(a) $A(t)\in\mathcal B(H)$ with $A(0)=A$, $\|A(t)\|=\|A\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]) and $A(t)^{*}=A^{*}(t)$; in particular $A$ self-adjoint implies every $A(t)$ self-adjoint ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). Moreover $A(t+s)=U(s)^{*}A(t)U(s)$ for all $s,t$.

(b) If $A\,D(T)\subseteq D(T)$, then $A(t)D(T)\subseteq D(T)$ for every $t$, and for every $x\in D(T)$ the map $t\mapsto A(t)x$ is differentiable at every $t$ with
$$\frac{d}{dt}A(t)x=-i\,[T,A(t)]x=-i\bigl(TA(t)-A(t)T\bigr)x .$$

(c) For every $x\in H$ the map $t\mapsto A(t)x$ is continuous, and the uniform operator norm bound $\|A(t)\|\le\|A\|$ holds.

(d) If $A$ is self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]), then every $A(t)$ is self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure
$$E_{A(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
and the spectra agree, $\sigma(A(t))=\sigma(A)$.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Sections 3.1-3.2, printed pages 18-22 (Heisenberg operators and the Heisenberg equation of motion)

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 4.4, printed pages 70-71 (the Heisenberg picture: definition of the time-dependent operator, equation of motion, and equality of expectation values with the Schroedinger picture)

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.1, printed pages 55-58, and Theorems 5.1-5.2, printed pages 123-125 (domain invariance and differentiability of the unitary flow)

items.title: Stationary rays of a self-adjoint flow are exactly the eigenrays
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]), let $T$ be self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) with spectral projection-valued measure $E$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]), let $U(t)=e^{itT}=\int e^{it\lambda}\,dE(\lambda)$ be the generated strongly continuous unitary group ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]], [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]), and let $\psi\in H$ with $\psi\ne0$. Then the following are equivalent:

(i) for every $t\in\mathbb R$ the vector $U(t)\psi$ is a complex multiple of $\psi$ (the ray of $\psi$ is invariant under the flow);

(ii) $\psi\in D(T)$ and $T\psi=\lambda\psi$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ (the ray of $\psi$ is an eigenray of $T$).

If these hold for the eigenvalue $\lambda$, then $U(t)\psi=e^{it\lambda}\psi$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 3.1, printed pages 87-93 (the spectral theorem and the bounded functional calculus, including the identity ||P(f)psi||^2 = int |f|^2 d mu_psi), and Theorems 5.1-5.2, printed pages 123-125 (self-adjoint generators, domain invariance and the derivative characterization)
B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 3.1, printed pages 18-20 (Heisenberg operators, conservation and stationary states)

items.title: Assigned energy observable, unitary flow and the two pictures of autonomous evolution
items.statement:
**(a) Assigned energy observable.** Adopt the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4) for a declared isolated system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned energy observable** of the system is an assigned sharp observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), whose declared unit $u_H$ is an energy unit in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (joules in the SI conventions fixed there). Thus $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ is densely defined and self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ under the choice hypotheses of [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and its outcome law in a preparation is the law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). The assignment of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is part of the model specification, as in clause (i) of P4; this definition asserts nothing about which laboratory quantity of a concrete system realizes it.

**(b) The unitary flow.** The **time evolution** or **flow** of the isolated system is the family
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P4 in the spectral calculus of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); here $\hbar>0$ is the reduced Planck constant with its value and unit fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], so that $tH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ is dimensionless. Equivalently, $U(t)=e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint generator $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; the two readings agree by the uniqueness of the generator in Stone's theorem, and by [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]] ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)) the family $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

**(c) Schroedinger picture.** The **Schroedinger-picture evolution** of a preparation is fixed by clause (iii) of P4. A state vector evolves by $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the **state at time $t$** of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ is the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$, which is well defined because $U(t)$ is injective; a general preparation $\rho$, that is an element of the state space $D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], evolves by
$$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
the reading of clause (iii) of P4 in the density-operator vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). In this picture the assigned observables are held fixed at their assigned values and the preparation moves.

**(d) Heisenberg picture.** For a **bounded** assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ — that is, an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]), so that $A$ is self-adjoint and everywhere defined — the **Heisenberg representative** of $(A,u_A)$ at time $t$ is the pair $(A_H(t),u_A)$ with the same declared unit and
$$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t).$$
By [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), $A_H(t)$ is again bounded and self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$, so $(A_H(t),u_A)$ is again an assigned sharp observable of the framework; in this picture the preparation is held fixed at its value at time $0$ and the observables move. The two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; the statement that they assign the same outcome laws is proved in the Heisenberg-picture theorem of this page, not assumed here.

**(e) Stationary preparations.** A preparation $\rho\in D(H)$ is **stationary** for the assigned energy observable when $\rho(t)=\rho$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. A pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary when $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, that is, when the evolved vector remains in the ray of $\psi$; the characterization of this condition by the eigenrays of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is proved in the stationary-states theorem of this page, not assumed here. An **energy eigenstate** is a pure preparation of a unit eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$, and a **stationary state** in the model is a stationary pure preparation; by that theorem the two notions coincide.

**(f) Energy-compatible observables.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ is **compatible with the energy**, or **energy-compatible**, when its spectral projection-valued measure and that of the energy commute strongly,
$$E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)\qquad\text{for all Borel }B,C\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is an equality of bounded operators on $H$, not a relation between formal commutators on a small domain; the phrase **conserved quantity** for an energy-compatible assigned observable is a claim about the time invariance of its outcome law and is established in the energy-conservation theorem of this page for bounded $A$.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P4 together with P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P4, P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematics, assert no dynamics for a prescribed time-dependent family or for an open system (clauses (iv) and (v) of P4 are separate model assumptions treated on their own pages), assert no measurement model, no apparatus realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any laboratory system is exactly isolated.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.1, printed pages 55-58, and Theorems 5.1-5.2, printed pages 123-125 (self-adjoint observables, the unitary group they generate and the domain-qualified Schroedinger equation)

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Sections 2.1-3.2, printed pages 10-22 (unitary time evolution, the evolution operator, Heisenberg operators and the Heisenberg equation)

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 2.2 and 4.3-4.4, printed pages 21-23 and 68-71 (time evolution, conserved quantities, stationary states and the Heisenberg picture)

items.physical_scope: The evolution vocabulary of the framework's autonomous-dynamics postulate P4: the assigned energy observable and its unit, the unitary flow it generates, the Schroedinger-picture evolution of state vectors and density operators, the Heisenberg-picture representative of a bounded assigned sharp observable, stationarity of pure preparations, and compatibility (conservation) of an assigned sharp observable with the energy. This item fixes readings and terminology of P4 together with P1 and P2; it adopts no assumption beyond those postulates and the cited mathematics, asserts no evolution for driven or open systems, no measurement or apparatus realization, no isolation claim about any laboratory system, and no empirical result.

items.title: The Schroedinger-picture flow: unitarity, domain invariance and the domain-qualified equation
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. Let $H$ be the state space assigned to a declared isolated system of the massive-matter sector ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), let $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ be its assigned energy observable with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (a)), and let
$$U(t)=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda),\qquad \psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0),\qquad \rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$$
be the flow and the state evolutions of clauses (b) and (c) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], with $\hbar>0$ and the energy unit in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Then:

(a) **Unitary flow.** $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]) with $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$ and $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$; every orbit has constant norm, $\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi(0)\|$, so for $\psi(0)\ne0$ the ray $[\psi(t)]$ is a pure preparation of the model for every $t$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

(b) **Domain invariance.** $U(t)D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ for every $t$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}U(t)=U(t)H_{\mathrm{op}}$ on $D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$: the flow preserves the energy domain and commutes with the energy there.

(c) **Schroedinger equation on the domain.** For $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ the curve $t\mapsto\psi(t)$ is norm-differentiable at every $t\in\mathbb R$, it stays in $D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, and
$$i\hbar\,\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(t)=H_{\mathrm{op}}U(t)\psi(0);$$
for $\psi(0)\in H\setminus D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ the curve is norm-differentiable at no $t\in\mathbb R$, so the equation is not asserted there, although the evolution $t\mapsto\psi(t)$ remains continuous.

(d) **Density-operator evolution.** For every preparation $\rho$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]) and every $t$ the operator $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ is again a preparation: self-adjoint, positive, trace class with $\operatorname{tr}\rho(t)=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). Moreover for every bounded operator $B$ the identity $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)B\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)U(t)^{*}BU(t)\bigr)$ holds.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1 and P4 and the cited mathematics. They assert no evolution for a prescribed time-dependent Hamiltonian, no non-unitary reduced dynamics, no measurement, apparatus or detector model, no claim that any laboratory system is isolated, and no empirical result.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Theorems 5.1-5.2, printed pages 123-125 (the unitary group generated by a self-adjoint operator, invariance of the domain and the domain-qualified Schroedinger equation)

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Sections 2.1-2.2, printed pages 10-15 (unitary time evolution, composition and inverses of the evolution operator, and the Schroedinger equation)
D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted complete lecture set), Section 1.2, printed pages 9-13 (the Schroedinger equation and the conservation of total probability)

items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the state and composition postulate P1 and the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 for a declared isolated system of the framework: the flow generated by the assigned energy observable is a strongly continuous unitary group, it preserves the operator domain and commutes with the energy there, the Schroedinger equation holds in the norm-differentiable sense exactly on the domain, and the evolution of a density-operator preparation is a trace-one density operator at every time. The item asserts no dynamics for driven or open systems, no measurement or apparatus realization, no isolation claim about any laboratory system and no empirical result; all statements are conditional on P1 and P4 and on the cited mathematics.

items.title: The Heisenberg picture: equivalent predictions and the domain-qualified equation of motion
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] (P2), and the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ be the assigned energy observable of a declared isolated system with state space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]) and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ as in [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and let $(A,u_A)$ be a bounded assigned sharp observable: $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ is self-adjoint everywhere defined ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]) with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Put
$$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$
Then:

(a) **The Heisenberg representative is an assigned sharp observable.** For every $t$, $A_H(t)$ is bounded and self-adjoint with $\|A_H(t)\|=\|A\|$ and spectrum $\sigma(A_H(t))=\sigma(A)$, and its spectral projection-valued measure is
$$E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel});$$
with the declared unit $u_A$ it is again a bounded assigned sharp observable of the framework, and $A_H(0)=A$.

(b) **The two pictures assign the same laws.** For every preparation $\rho$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A_H(t)}_{\rho(0)}(B),$$
where $\mu^{\cdot}_{\cdot}$ is the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$; for the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ this reads $\|E_A(B)U(t)\psi\|^{2}=\|E_{A_H(t)}(B)\psi\|^{2}$. In particular the expectation value of the bounded observable agrees, $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)A_H(t)\bigr)$.

(c) **Heisenberg equation.** If $A\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subseteq D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, then for every $x\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ the curve $t\mapsto A_H(t)x$ is differentiable at every $t$ and
$$i\hbar\,\frac{d}{dt}A_H(t)x=\bigl[A_H(t),H_{\mathrm{op}}\bigr]x=\bigl(A_H(t)H_{\mathrm{op}}-H_{\mathrm{op}}A_H(t)\bigr)x .$$

(d) **Energy-compatible observables are frozen.** If $A$ is compatible with the energy, that is $E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)$ for all Borel $B,C$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (f)), then $A_H(t)=A$ for every $t$, and by (b) the outcome law of $(A,u_A)$ is the same in $\rho(t)$ as in $\rho(0)$ for every preparation.

(e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1, P2 and P4 and the cited mathematics. They introduce no new physical assumption, no measurement or apparatus model, no collapse, no driven or open dynamics; they make no claim about which laboratory quantity realizes $(A,u_A)$ and record no empirical result.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Sections 3.1-3.2, printed pages 18-22 (Heisenberg operators, their properties, and the Heisenberg equation of motion)

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 4.4, printed pages 70-71 (the Heisenberg picture: the time-dependent operator, its equation of motion and the equality of expectation values with the Schroedinger picture)
G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.1, printed pages 55-58 (self-adjoint observables and their spectral measures)

items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of this page for a declared isolated system: the Heisenberg representative of a bounded assigned sharp observable is again a bounded assigned sharp observable with the same unit, norm and spectrum, the two pictures assign the same outcome laws to every preparation, the domain-qualified Heisenberg equation holds, and energy-compatible bounded observables are frozen in the Heisenberg picture. No measurement, apparatus, detector, driven-dynamics or open-system claim is made, and no empirical result is asserted.

items.title: Energy conservation, conserved sharp observables and the stationary eigenrays
items.statement:
Adopt the state and composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] (P2), and the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ be the assigned energy observable of a declared isolated system with state space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]), and write $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$. Then:

(a) **Energy law and moments.** For every preparation $\rho$, every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(t)E_H(B)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(0)E_H(B)\bigr)=\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\rho(0)}(B);$$
for the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ likewise $\|E_H(B)U(t)\psi\|^{2}=\|E_H(B)\psi\|^{2}$. If $\psi(0)\ne0$ and $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, the mean and second moment of the energy law of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ are finite and time-independent. For any nonzero representative $\psi(0)$ their time-zero values are
$$\frac{\langle H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(0),\psi(0)\rangle}{\|\psi(0)\|^{2}}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\frac{\|H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(0)\|^{2}}{\|\psi(0)\|^{2}},$$
respectively. The displayed conservation of moments makes no assertion that these moments are finite for preparations outside this domain hypothesis.

(b) **Conserved sharp observables.** Let $(A,u_A)$ be a bounded assigned sharp observable that is compatible with the energy ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (f)). Then its outcome law is time-independent: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel set $B$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B).$$

(c) **Stationary states are exactly the eigenrays.** Let $\psi\in H$, $\psi\ne0$. The pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary, that is $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, if and only if $\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$: $\psi\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ and $H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi=\lambda\psi$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. In that case $\psi(t)=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\psi(0)$ for every $t$, and every assigned sharp observable has a time-independent outcome law in this preparation: $\mu^{A}_{[\psi(t)]}(B)=\mu^{A}_{[\psi(0)]}(B)$ for every $(A,u_A)$, every Borel $B$ and every $t$.

(d) **Status and exclusions.** No equilibration, relaxation, decay or convergence of the law of an arbitrary preparation is asserted; no moment beyond those finite at time zero is claimed; the converse of (b) — constancy of the law of a bounded observable in every preparation implying strong spectral compatibility with the energy — is not asserted for a general (possibly unbounded) $H_{\mathrm{op}}$; and the item is conditional on the isolated-system idealization of P4, asserting no apparatus realization and no empirical result.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 5.1, printed pages 123-125, equation (5.4) on printed page 124 (time-independent expectations of the energy: conservation of energy), and Theorem 8.1, printed page 174 (a self-adjoint operator commuting with H is a conserved quantity with invariant domain)
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 2.2.1, printed pages 23-24 (Ehrenfest's theorem, conserved quantities and the conservation of the expectation of the energy)

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Sections 2.1 and 3.2, printed pages 10-17 and 20-22 (norm conservation, Heisenberg operators and operators constant in time when they commute with the Hamiltonian)

items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of this page for a declared isolated system: the outcome law of the assigned energy observable is time-independent in every preparation; for a pure preparation represented by a nonzero vector in the energy domain, its finite first and second energy moments, evaluated on a unit representative, are conserved; every bounded assigned sharp observable compatible with the energy has a time-independent outcome law; and a pure preparation is stationary exactly when it is an eigenray of the energy, in which case all its outcome laws are time-independent. No relaxation, equilibration or decay is asserted; no converse of the compatibility criterion is claimed for unbounded energy operators; no measurement, apparatus or empirical claim is made.

items.title: What the autonomous-dynamics page adopts, proves and does not claim
items.statement:
**What the page adopts.** The single physical assumption materialized here is the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), read in the vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] for an isolated system of the framework with state space of the type fixed by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. In particular the assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$, its energy unit and the reduced Planck constant entering the phase are model specifications in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; no numerical value of any of them is produced by this page.

**What is proved.** [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-schrodinger-picture-flow]] draws, from P4 and the local mathematics [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]], the unitary flow, the invariance of the energy domain, the domain-qualified Schroedinger equation and the evolution of density-operator preparations. [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-picture]], using [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]], identifies the Heisenberg representative of a bounded assigned sharp observable and proves that the two pictures assign the same outcome laws, together with the domain-qualified Heisenberg equation and the freezing of energy-compatible bounded observables. [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] reads the conservation of the energy law and its finite moments, the conservation of any bounded energy-compatible observable, and the equivalence of stationary pure preparations with the eigenrays of the energy; the mathematical core of that equivalence is [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-ray-characterization]]. All statements are conditional consequences of the adopted postulates and the cited mathematics; none of them is an empirical claim.

**What is not claimed.** (i) The page treats only the autonomous case: a prescribed time-dependent family $t\mapsto H(t)$ and the propagator problems it raises are not covered by P4(ii) and are deferred to the driven-dynamics development, and an open or reduced non-unitary evolution is an extension requiring an environment model, in the sense of clauses (iv) and (v) of P4. (ii) No measurement, collapse, conditioning or apparatus model is introduced; the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] is used only to read statistics of a preparation, and the state after an outcome is not treated. (iii) No relaxation, equilibration or convergence of the law of a general preparation is asserted. (iv) The converse of the conservation criterion — that a bounded observable whose law is constant in every preparation must be strongly spectrally compatible with the energy — is not proved for a general possibly unbounded $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ and is therefore not claimed. (v) The equation of motion is asserted exactly on the operator domain; for vectors outside the domain only the unitary flow, not the differential equation, is available.

**Empirical status.** Whether a concrete laboratory system realizes P4's isolated-system idealization, and whether a concrete apparatus realizes a preparation of the type used here, are tested identifications with uncertainty, in the sense of the framework's preparation and apparatus assumptions; they are not consequences of P4. This pair records no measurement, apparatus, calibration or data, and the worked companion page contains finite model computations only.

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.1, printed pages 55-58 (the physical axioms are assumptions; self-adjoint dynamics is a mathematical consequence of the operator hypothesis)

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted complete lecture set), Section 1.2, printed pages 9-14 (the Schroedinger equation as an adopted equation of motion, and the conservation of total probability)

The remark asserts no dynamics, reports no measurement and records no empirical data.

items.title: Precession of a two-level preparation: exact phases, probabilities and a Bloch-vector rotation
items.statement:
Let $H=\mathbb C^{2}$ carry the standard inner product $\langle z,w\rangle=z_{1}\overline{w_{1}}+z_{2}\overline{w_{2}}$ ([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]), with orthonormal basis $u_{1}=(1,0)$, $u_{2}=(0,1)$ and rank-one calculus $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]). Fix two distinct energies $E_{1}\ne E_{2}$ in joules (model parameters, not measured values), and consider the assigned energy observable of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (a),
$$H_{\mathrm{op}}:=E_{1}T_{u_{1},u_{1}}+E_{2}T_{u_{2},u_{2}},\qquad u_{H}=\mathrm J,$$
of an isolated system whose state space is the two-level state space of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. Define the bounded self-adjoint observables
$$X:=T_{u_{1},u_{2}}+T_{u_{2},u_{1}},\qquad Y:=iT_{u_{2},u_{1}}-iT_{u_{1},u_{2}},\qquad Z:=T_{u_{1},u_{1}}-T_{u_{2},u_{2}},$$
with the same dimensionless unit, and let $\psi_{0}=\alpha u_{1}+\beta u_{2}$ be a unit vector. Writing
$$\omega:=\frac{E_{2}-E_{1}}{\hbar}\quad(\text{units }\mathrm s^{-1}),$$
the example establishes the following exact model statements.

(i) The spectral projection-valued measure of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is $E_{H}(B)=\mathbf 1_{E_{1}\in B}T_{u_{1},u_{1}}+\mathbf 1_{E_{2}\in B}T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$, and the flow is $U(t)=e^{-iE_{1}t/\hbar}T_{u_{1},u_{1}}+e^{-iE_{2}t/\hbar}T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$.

(ii) $X,Y,Z$ are bounded self-adjoint with $X^{2}=Y^{2}=Z^{2}=I$ and $XY=iZ$; their spectra are $\{\pm1\}$, with $Y$ and $Z$ obtained from $X$ by the same pattern.

(iii) The evolved preparation is $\psi(t)=U(t)\psi_{0}=\alpha e^{-iE_{1}t/\hbar}u_{1}+\beta e^{-iE_{2}t/\hbar}u_{2}$, of unit norm, and the expectations are
$$\langle X\rangle(t)=2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\alpha\overline{\beta}\,e^{i\omega t}\bigr),\qquad \langle Y\rangle(t)=-2\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\alpha\overline{\beta}\,e^{i\omega t}\bigr),\qquad \langle Z\rangle(t)=|\alpha|^{2}-|\beta|^{2}.$$

(iv) The triple $v(t):=\bigl(\langle X\rangle(t),\langle Y\rangle(t),\langle Z\rangle(t)\bigr)\in\mathbb R^{3}$ has constant norm one and is the rotation of $v(0)$ about the third axis by the angle $-\omega t$: $v(t)=R_{3}(-\omega t)v(0)$, where $R_{3}(\theta)(x,y,z)=(x\cos\theta-y\sin\theta,\ x\sin\theta+y\cos\theta,\ z)$. Thus the expectation-value triple precesses with angular frequency $\omega$.

(v) The outcome law of $X$ in the preparation $[\psi(t)]$ is the two-point law $\mu^{X}_{\psi(t)}(\{+1\})=(1+\langle X\rangle(t))/2$, $\mu^{X}_{\psi(t)}(\{-1\})=(1-\langle X\rangle(t))/2$; in particular for $\alpha=\beta=1/\sqrt{2}$ one has $\mu^{X}_{\psi(t)}(\{+1\})=(1+\cos\omega t)/2$.

(vi) The energy law is time-independent, $\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\psi(t)}(\{E_{1}\})=|\alpha|^{2}$ and $\mu^{H_{\mathrm{op}}}_{\psi(t)}(\{E_{2}\})=|\beta|^{2}$ for every $t$, and every one of the displayed expectations is periodic in $t$ with period $2\pi/|\omega|$ (when $\omega\ne0$, which holds because $E_{1}\ne E_{2}$).

The computation is a model-internal one: the energies are parameters of the assigned observable, the probabilities are those of the framework's outcome law, and no laboratory measurement, apparatus or empirical value is asserted.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 7 'Two State Systems', Sections 2-3, chapter pages 2-6 (spin precession and the general time-independent two-state Hamiltonian with its precession frequency)

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 2.2, printed pages 21-23 (energy eigenstates acquire phases e^{-iEt/hbar}; general states evolve as finite superpositions with time-dependent relative phases)

items.physical_scope: A finite, exact model computation in the two-level state space of the framework: the assigned energy observable with two distinct energies in joules, its unitary flow, the exact evolution of a pure preparation, the outcome laws and expectations of three bounded self-adjoint observables, the resulting rotation of the expectation-value triple, and the explicit period of the laws. The energies are model parameters; the item asserts no apparatus realization, no detection model and no empirical value, and it identifies the two-level system with no specific physical species.

items.title: A finite superposition of energy eigenrays: exact phases, laws and return times
items.statement:
Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be the state space of a declared isolated system of the framework ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), let $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ be its assigned energy observable with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]), and let $u_{1},\dots,u_{N}$ be a finite orthonormal family of eigenvectors of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ with real eigenvalues $\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{N}$: $H_{\mathrm{op}}u_{n}=\lambda_{n}u_{n}$ for $n=1,\dots,N$. Fix coefficients $c_{n}\in\mathbb C$ and the nonzero vector
$$\psi_{0}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}c_{n}u_{n},\qquad S:=\{n:c_{n}\ne0\}.$$
For a nonzero vector $\phi$, write $\mu^{A}_{[\phi]}$ for the outcome law of the pure preparation $[\phi]$, computed on the unit representative $\phi/\|\phi\|$ as in [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b) and [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]].
Then, with $\psi(t)=U(t)\psi_{0}$:

(i) $\psi(t)=\sum_{n\in S}c_{n}e^{-i\lambda_{n}t/\hbar}u_{n}$ for every $t$, and $\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi_{0}\|$; if $S$ has one element, or more generally if all $\lambda_{n}$ with $n\in S$ coincide, the ray $[\psi(t)]$ is constant.

(ii) For every bounded assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ and every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, the outcome law in the preparation $[\psi(t)]$ is
$$\mu^{A}_{[\psi(t)]}(B)=\frac{1}{\|\psi_{0}\|^{2}}\sum_{m,n\in S}c_{n}\overline{c_{m}}\,e^{-i(\lambda_{n}-\lambda_{m})t/\hbar}\,\langle E_{A}(B)u_{n},u_{m}\rangle .$$
Thus the probability is a finite trigonometric polynomial in $t$ with frequencies $(\lambda_{n}-\lambda_{m})/\hbar$.

(iii) For $T>0$ the following are equivalent: (a) $[\psi(t+T)]=[\psi(t)]$ for every $t$; (b) $e^{-i\lambda_{n}T/\hbar}$ is independent of $n\in S$; (c) $(\lambda_{m}-\lambda_{n})T/\hbar\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ for all $m,n\in S$.

(iv) Consequently a positive return time exists if and only if there are $\omega_{0}>0$ and integers $k_{n}$ ($n\in S$) with $(\lambda_{n}-\lambda_{n_{0}})/\hbar=\omega_{0}k_{n}$ for all $n\in S$, where $n_{0}$ is any fixed element of $S$; and then $T=2\pi/\omega_{0}$ is a return time.

(v) Two-energy case $N=2$, $\lambda_{1}\ne\lambda_{2}$, $c_{1}c_{2}\ne0$: the positive return times are exactly $T=2\pi\hbar k/|\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}|$, $k=1,2,3,\dots$; the least return time is $2\pi\hbar/|\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}|$, which is the period $2\pi/|\omega|$ of the precession example with $\omega=(\lambda_{2}-\lambda_{1})/\hbar$.

(vi) In the stationary case of (i), every outcome law of every assigned sharp observable is independent of $t$: $\mu^{A}_{[\psi(t)]}(B)=\mu^{A}_{[\psi(0)]}(B)$.

The computation is a model-internal one: the eigenvalues are parameters of the assigned observable, and no identification with a physical spectrum, apparatus or measured value is asserted.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 2.2, printed pages 21-23 (equation (2.32): the evolution of a general state as a superposition of energy eigenstates with relative phases e^{-iE_n t/hbar})

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 2.3, printed pages 15-17 (the evolution operator for a time-independent Hamiltonian and its application to eigenstates)

items.physical_scope: A finite, exact model computation for a declared isolated system: the evolution of a nonzero finite superposition of orthogonal energy eigenrays, the resulting trigonometric-polynomial form of the outcome laws of bounded assigned sharp observables, the exact return-time criterion for the ray, the two-energy period, and the stationary case. The eigenvalues are model parameters; the item asserts no apparatus, no detection model and no empirical value, and no finite set of energies is identified with a physical spectrum.

items.title: A superposition of distinct energy eigenrays need not be stationary
items.statement: Adopt the autonomous-dynamics reading of the framework ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics|P4]]). Then: **every** preparation of an isolated system that is a superposition of two or more energy eigenrays with distinct eigenvalues is a stationary state, in the sense that all of its outcome laws are independent of time; in particular a superposition of two eigenrays of the two-level model is stationary.

references.title: B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 7 'Two State Systems', Sections 2-3, chapter pages 2-6 (two-state precession: superpositions of energy eigenstates with distinct energies have time-dependent expectation values, while eigenstates do not)

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 2.2 and 2.2.1, printed pages 21-24 (only states of well-defined energy have time-independent expectation values of all time-independent operators; superpositions generally do not)

items.physical_scope: A refutation, inside the framework's autonomous-dynamics reading, of the informal claim that every superposition of two or more distinct energy eigenrays of an isolated system is a stationary state with time-independent outcome laws: in the explicit two-level model with two distinct energies, an equal-weight superposition carries the bounded flip observable with an outcome probability oscillating between one and zero. The item refutes that specific universal claim; it asserts no apparatus, no measurement statistics from a laboratory and no empirical result, and it does not deny that individual eigenrays are stationary or that special superpositions can be stationary.

items.title: What the worked items of the companion page establish
items.statement:
**Two-level precession.** [[ex-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-two-level-precession]] computes, on the explicit two-dimensional state space, the spectral measure and flow of the assigned energy observable $E_{1}T_{u_{1},u_{1}}+E_{2}T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$ with $E_{1}\ne E_{2}$, the exact phases of an evolved preparation, the outcome probabilities and expectations of three bounded observables, and the rotation of the expectation-value triple about the third axis with angular frequency $\omega=(E_{2}-E_{1})/\hbar$. The computation verifies the flow and law of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] on finite data, and it confirms the energy conservation of [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] clause (a) in the model. No apparatus realization, detector resolution or measured frequency is asserted.

**Finite superpositions.** [[ex-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-finite-stationary-superposition]] computes the evolution of a nonzero finite superposition of orthogonal energy eigenrays, the trigonometric-polynomial form of the outcome laws of a bounded assigned sharp observable, the exact return-time criterion $(\lambda_{m}-\lambda_{n})T/\hbar\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ for $m,n$ in the support of the coefficients, the existence criterion for a positive return time via a common frequency, and the two-energy specialization with least return time $2\pi\hbar/|\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}|$. These are exact model statements under the flow of [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-schrodinger-picture-flow]].

**A failed universal claim.** [[cex-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-superposition-with-distinct-energies-is-not-stationary]] refutes the informal universal statement that every superposition of distinct energy eigenrays is stationary: on the two-level model with $\psi_{0}=(u_{1}+u_{2})/\sqrt2$ the outcome law of the flip observable takes the values $1$ at $t=0$ and $0$ at $t=\pi/|\omega|$. The refutation isolates the relative phase as the mechanism and is consistent with the exact stationarity criterion of [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] clause (c): the individual eigenrays are stationary, the equal-weight superposition of distinct eigenrays is not.

## What the page does not establish

None of the three items is an experiment: no counts, calibration, resolution, efficiency, background, uncertainty or data comparison appears anywhere on the page, and no energy value is measured. The two-level system is an abstract model and is not identified with a spin, a magnetic moment, a photon polarization or any other species; the coupling of spin to a magnetic field belongs to the corresponding model pages, and driven or resonant dynamics is deferred to the driven-dynamics development, which adopts its own time-dependent assumptions. The return-time and precession results are statements about the model's flow and outcome law, not about the stability, decoherence or control of any laboratory preparation.

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 2.2 and 4.4, printed pages 21-23 and 70-71 (superpositions of energy eigenstates and the Heisenberg picture)
